newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: High demand season to dampen Thai gasoline exports.
newsitem.headline: High demand season to dampen Thai gasoline exports.

text.p: Thailand's gasoline exports are expected to fall from January as domestic consumption during the high demand season of the first quarter absorbs most of its surplus output, industry sources said on Thursday.
"Demand for gasoline, gas oil (diesel) and aviation jet fuel usually increases from February during the Chinese New Year holiday travelling," a Thai refiner told Reuters.
The sources said only one refiner, Thai Oil Co Ltd, has export availabilities in January.
Sources at Caltex and Royal Dutch Shell said they had no spot cargoes to sell in January because they were reserving their stocks for the local market.
Traders said Thai Oil is offering up to 250,000 barrels of 95-octane gasoline for export in mid-December through a tender which was offered to selected customers. The tender closes on December 6.
But even Thai Oil plans to cut its normal monthly exports to one from its usual two cargoes in January, and will not have any export supplies in February and March, the sources said.
"Normally, demand by March is high," said a source at state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT). "But you never know...it (the export market) is subject to domestic demand and supply."

The startup of additional refining capacities this year has enabled Thailand to export more gasoline in recent months despite strong annual domestic demand growth of around nine to 10 percent. Thailand consumed around 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of gasoline between January and September this year.
Shell and Caltex, the joint venture between U.S. giants Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, have boosted Thailand's refining capacity by 275,000-bpd to 760,000-bpd.

Since July, the new facilities and existing refiners such as Thai Oil started to export up to three million barrels a month of petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

For the first time, two refiners each concluded one-year term contracts to export 240,000-barrel cargoes of gasoline a quarter. A third supplies 125,000-to-170,000 barrels of gasoline a month to Vietnam, the sources said.

Thai exports have contributed to a squeeze in refinery profits in the region, traders said. As a result, Thai refiners had to reduce refinery operating rates by 10-15 percent between October and November when demand was low in the monsoon season.
Thai refiners were now expected to raise their output to take advantage of current high international prices.
"Shell has not been affected that much by weak (refining) margins...there has not been that much exports," said a trading source.

"With a bigger (retail) market share than Caltex, the highest yield (for Shell Thailand) has been the domestic gasoline market. Domestic prices are quite immune from international prices," the source said.
